proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a coloring f satisfying the hypothesis that the circumcenter of any noncollinear monochromatic triple has the same color. By Lemma L4, some color class contains a noncollinear triple; call the color c, and call the triple A,B,C. By Lemma L1, the color class S_c = {P : f(P)=c} is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples from S_c. Since A,B,C are noncollinear points of S_c, Lemma L5 applies and yields S_c = R^2. Unwinding the definition of S_c, every point of the plane has color c. Therefore the coloring is constant, which is exactly the theorem.

steps.derives: There exists a color c in {red,green} and points A,B,C in R^2 such that f(A)=f(B)=f(C)=c and A,B,C are noncollinear.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L4 directly to the given coloring f.

steps.derives: For the color c obtained in step A1, the set S_c = {P in R^2 : f(P)=c} is closed under circumcenters of noncollinear triples of its points.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of Lemma L1 applied to f and the chosen color c.

steps.derives: The points A,B,C from step A1 all belong to S_c, and they are noncollinear.
steps.trivial_justification: By definition of S_c, the equalities f(A)=f(B)=f(C)=c imply A,B,C are elements of S_c; noncollinearity was part of step A1.

Lemma L5 applies because step A2 gives the required circumcenter-closure property for S_c, and step A3 provides a noncollinear triple of points lying in S_c. Therefore every point of R^2 belongs to S_c.

steps.derives: For every point P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: Since S_c = R^2 and S_c was defined as {P : f(P)=c}, every point P lies in S_c, hence f(P)=c.

steps.derives: There exists a color c in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A5 exhibits the required witness c and proves the universal statement for that c.
